newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu loses confidence vote but stays in power.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu loses confidence vote but stays in power.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lost a parliamentary no-confidence vote on Monday but stayed in office as opposition parties failed to rally enough support to topple his government.
The vote in the 120-member parliament went 49-44 against Netanyahu on a no-confidence motion over rising unemployment presented by the opposition Labour and Meretz parties.
Bringing down the government requires an absolute majority of 61 legislators.

Netanyahu's coalition partners from the National Religious Party stayed away from the vote in a tiff with the prime minister over the appointment of religious officials, tipping the scales in the opposition's favour.
Disgruntled legislators in Netanyahu's 66-member coalition have helped the opposition narrow the gap in a series of recent no-confidence votes.
